areas.label: Recover actor and rendering initialization
areas.evidence: The palette result is stored through a local u16 pointer to the palette global (loads the address into a callee-saved register before the call), and the wait is a plain while loop on the global. The player-history clear is for (i = 0 ...) with s16 counters. The ground position is a local s32 ground[2]: a two-word aggregate pseudo keeps both initial stores (X and the constant 0x6800 Y) and gets the 8-byte slot at SP+0x50, giving the original 148-byte frame.

areas.label: Recover the real main loop and state switch
areas.evidence: The state switch is fully structured C with every tail written out (no gotos); jump2 cross-jumping reproduces the shared tails once register allocation matches. The actor uses a struct type (Act4D08) so stores through it do not alias the scalar object pointer global, and players are a 0x14C-byte struct array; player coordinates are copied as players[id()].x = players[id()].x2 = v. Constant fC stores go through one u16 local (arg0->fC = state = K) so they share one callee-saved register. Locals use their natural narrow types (u16 hitTimer/shotTimer/lastAnim, s16 shake, u8 pattern/wave). The sine table read goes through an s32 temporary (keeps ldrsh with a zero index register, which also fixes reload-register rotation for the rest of the function), and the pattern update is a u8 ?: expression.
